github.body:
AI late-game insolvency after #933: the subsidy bill on ports, railways and policy-forced renewables
Follow-up to #933. #980 and #981 removed the AI's power-plant subsidies, but the AI stayed insolvent, because its subsidy bill moved to other buildings. The owner closed #933 as done for power plants (2026-10-18) and asked for this issue to cover the rest.

hackernews.author: hn_acker
hackernews.body:
Canadians are running out of time to oppose Bill C-22
The petition to withdraw and amend the bill was presented to the House of Commons today [1]. People whining about how there's nothing they can do basically don't engage in democracy and thats how you end up in a US situation..
[1] https://www.ourcommons.ca/petitions/en/Petition/Details?Peti... If the bill isn't dramatically changed or killed, all the major messaging services along with tons of other services will end up blocking Canada. It's very rare for the senate to kill a bill. I would say that we alreadt ran out of time.

hackernews.author: guiambros
hackernews.body:
NY announces game ownership bill requiring ownership rather than licensing
The headline makes it sound like this is specific to NY, but this is a national bill introduced in the House by a NY rep. Even better would be broad copyright reforms. Fair Use needs to be expanded and clarified. History has shown players are able to keep games alive themselves by emulators, reverse engineering, custom servers, etc. Expand Fair Use to say that these things are protected if needed to keep the game funct... We should give our money to folks like GOG (www.gog.com) who provide DRM-free games, all downloadable and playable offline.  no need to be online.  No need to create an account. no need to play (heh) by someone else's rules.

hackernews.author: f-serif
hackernews.body:
Anthropic's proposed AI safety bill only kicks in if 50 deaths or $1B in damages
Proposal:
1. Prosecute and lock people up over known instances of AI-enabled hacking, so companies playing fast and loose know “oops my AI did it” isn’t a useful defense. Right now they even sort of wear it as a badge of honor.
2. If you’re actually worried about AI killing lots of people, you immed... All these "safety" bills are to stop open source models by painting them as "dangerous". Regulatory capture.
Companies are responsible for their agents; you don't blame the car for running over the person. The CoT must be delightful.
This action would easily kill over a hundred people, so can't proceed. This action doesn't kill anybody but losses are estimated at over 2 billion, can't proceed. This action kills only twenty but losses close to 1 billion, unsure, spawning subagent to check numbers. This...

comment_insights: Proposal:
All these "safety" bills are to stop open source models by painting them as "dangerous"
The CoT must be delightful.

The next step is demanding anyone who wishes to release a Certified Safe AI™ model to prove they can insure the $1B in damages and pass a compliance audit for how they will prevent the LTM death count
This seems to be a case where Anthropic just can't win in the public court, and the other big ones (Google, Microsoft) have realized it / don't care enough, so they are rather quiet
